en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as giant inclined planes, reducing the force needed for farmers to carry heavy harvests up the mountain.
The sharp, tapered edge of a traditional Filipino bolo acts as a wedge to easily split open hard coconuts.
The deep treads on jeepney tires increase friction against wet roads, preventing the vehicle from slipping during the rainy season.
The gravitational pull of the moon causes the high and low tides that fishermen observe daily in Manila Bay.
The black sand beaches of Cagayan province contain magnetite, a naturally magnetic iron ore that is strongly attracted to magnets.
The Burgos Wind Farm in Ilocos Norte uses giant turbines to convert the kinetic energy of wind into electricity.
Fireflies along Bohol’s Loboc River produce their own cold light through a chemical reaction inside their abdomens called bioluminescence.
Shouting inside the Puerto Princesa Underground River creates an echo because sound waves bounce off the hard limestone cave walls.
A metal kawali heats up quickly to fry adobo because metal is an excellent conductor of thermal energy.
A Philippine eagle perched high in a Dipterocarp forest possesses gravitational potential energy before diving down to catch prey.
The smooth, streamlined body of a bangus reduces water friction, allowing it to swim efficiently through the fishpens of Dagupan.
Copper wires are used in Philippine household electrical systems because copper is an excellent conductor that easily allows electric current to flow.
